text: A Script Include method, ChangeRequestUtils.getActiveChangesByRisk, is supposed to return every active Change Request at a given risk level. Reports say it's returning unexpected results — some Change Requests that should clearly match aren't showing up. Here's the method as written, and we're going to diagnose it using this chapter's tools, in the right order.

Before assuming the logic inside the loop is wrong, trace the query itself first. Right after gr.query runs, a gs.info call logs getRowCount — how many rows actually came back — along with the risk level that was passed in. That's the fastest first check, synchronous or not.

Filtering the System Log for source ChangeRequestUtils shows: query returned 0 rows for risk high. Zero rows, even though active Change Requests at that risk level definitely exist. That single log line rules out the while loop and the results.push call entirely — the bug has to be in the query itself.

Looking again at the encoded query string: active equals t-u-r-e. A typo. It should be active equals true. ServiceNow's encoded query parser doesn't throw an error for an unrecognized value like that — it simply never matches any record, since no record has a literal active value of ture. The query silently returns nothing.
The fix is one character: true instead of ture. That alone makes the query start matching the active Change Requests it was always supposed to find — nothing else in the method needed to change.

Fixing the typo isn't the finish line. Re-running the exact same gs.info trace one more time confirms the row count is no longer zero, and only then should the temporary logging get removed — leaving debug logging in production code just adds noise for the next person tracing a different problem.

That's the whole chapter in one worked bug: trace the query before the loop, read the log line that narrows the problem, spot the one-character typo, fix it, and verify before calling it done. Next up starts Chapter 7, the capstone: defining the reusable utilities your own Script Include library will be built from.
